tool_input.command: git check-ignore -v data/guren.test.db 2>&1; git status --porcelain data/ 2>&1

result:
It's fine — `git status` already showed no changes under `data/`, confirming it's ignored. No need to run further checks.

Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (6/6). Summary of the fix:

**`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`** — `update()` previously read the raw request JSON (`await this.request.json()`) and wrote it straight into `Post.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses both validation and the `fillable` allowlist. That let any client-supplied field, including `authorId`, overwrite the post. It now calls `this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` (the same schema `store()` uses — `title`/`excerpt`/`body`, required with the same length limits) and passes the validated data to `Post.update()` (not `forceUpdate`), which additionally enforces `Post.fillable = ['title', 'excerpt', 'body']` as defense in depth. This closes the mass-assignment hole, restores the "Title is required." validation on edits, and ensures unrelated fields like `createdAt` can never be written.

**`tests/PostController.test.ts`** — added a `posts.update` suite covering: an `authorId` in the body is ignored and ownership stays with the original author; extraneous fields (`createdAt`) aren't written; an empty title is rejected with `422` and leaves the post unchanged; and a non-author is still refused with `403`.
